programme_facts.value: Identify the organisation you will visit and obtain permission from the organisation as well as your line manager.

metadata.chunk_title: Staff Teaching and Training

programme_facts.value: Discuss the type of activities you wish to undertake and create a programme of activities in collaboration with the host organisation.
Complete the Staff Mobility agreement for Teaching or Training.

The partner institution will sign your agreement, your line manager signs off on the quality of the agreement and grants permission to travel. Do this at least 5 weeks prior to your intended travel date.
Submit your fully signed mobility agreement to staff.mobility@ul.ie and UL Global will sign the agreement regarding the administrative requirements.
Allow 10 working days for your contract to be issued.
80% of your grant payment will be made within 30 calendar days after the signature of the agreement by both parties.
Keep your boarding cards and submit copies along with a signed and stamped Certificate of Attendance from your host to staff.mobility@ul.ie within 10 days of your return from teaching/training.
Complete the final report which you will receive via email from a Europa.eu email address.
Your final grant payment will be made within 10 working days on receipt of all documentation.
Once your final grant payment is made, complete the Acknowledgement of Grant Receipt form and return it to staff.mobility@ul.ie.
Please check out the process map by downloading it here.

If you are interested in completing an Erasmus+ EU Staff Training mobility, attending a Staff Week organised by one of UL's partner universities may be a good option.

Staff Weeks are usually designed to give an overview of the host university's institution and departments, while bringing together teaching and non-teaching staff to share ideas and potentially establish connections for future collaboration.
Many university Staff Weeks are advertised on the IMOTION website: http://staffmobility.eu/
Please note that individual Staff Week participation costs are not covered under Erasmus+, with participants eligible to receive a travel grant and daily subsistence grant only under the Programme.

A university awarded with an Erasmus Charter for Higher Education or any public or private organisation such as: a small, medium or large enterprise (including social enterprises), a public body at local, regional or national level, a social partner or other representative of working life, including chambers of commerce, craft/professional associations and trade unions, a research institute, a foundation, a school/institute/educational centre, a non-profit organisation, association or NGO, a body providing career guidance, professional counselling, and information services.
